idiom_name: indirect enum with labeled associated values + exhaustive switch
implementation_notes: Swift enums are the language's irregular AST: every case declares its own labeled associated values (case binary(left: Expr, op: String, right: Expr)), indirect inserts the indirection recursion needs, and switch over such an enum is exhaustive by language rule. Node-specific operations are functions, computed properties or methods on the enum, and the classic class hierarchy is only needed when nodes must be reference types or mutated in place - the Swift book's indirect ArithmeticExpression is exactly this structure.
pitfalls: Enums are value types: passing or assigning a node copies it unless children are held behind reference storage, so large trees can be copied unexpectedly.
indirect boxes recursive cases on the heap (one allocation per recursive node), which a performance-sensitive pass may want to avoid by using an explicit class or arena representation.
